summary: Defines an extension to Service Location Protocol version 2 so a client can ask for a service's attributes to be included in the reply. This avoids extra round trips to learn all the details. It is on the standards track.

eli5.summary: Instead of asking where the printer is and then asking what it can do, you get both answers at once.

questions: what is the slp attribute list extension
how to reduce slp round trips
is the slp attrlist extension required
subtitle: An optional SLPv2 extension that lets a service reply carry the service's attributes, saving round trips.

tldr.problem: In SLPv2 a client learns where a service is in one exchange, but the service's attributes need further request and reply messages.
tldr.mechanism: The client attaches an empty Attribute List Extension (ID 0x0002) to its Service Request. A supporting agent returns one Attribute List Extension per URL Entry in the Service Reply.
tldr.outcome: A client can get all service information in one exchange. Support is OPTIONAL, and a reply without the extension tells the client to fall back to Attribute Requests.

facts.label: Empty request
facts.value: Service URL Length and Attribute List Length set to 0

today: RFC 3059 is a Proposed Standard and the metadata lists no RFC that obsoletes or updates it. It extends SLPv2 as defined in RFC 2608.

sections.title: The Extra Round Trips Problem
sections.content:
The Service Location Protocol, Version 2 (SLPv2, RFC 2608) lets a service be discovered in a single exchange: a User Agent (UA) sends a Service Request and a Directory Agent (DA) or Service Agent (SA) sends back a Service Reply. SLP keeps different classes of information in different messages, so the reply does not include the service's attributes.

To get the attributes, the UA has to send more messages. This RFC defines an extension that lets the UA ask for the attributes to ride along in the Service Reply, which removes the need for those extra round trips.
sections.eli5: It is like asking a shop where the toy aisle is, and then having to go back and ask what toys they have. This lets you get both answers in one visit.

sections.title: The Agents Involved
sections.content:
Three roles appear in the document. A User Agent works on the user's behalf to establish contact with some service. A Service Agent works on behalf of one or more services to advertise them. A Directory Agent collects service advertisements, and there can only be one DA present per given host.

The UA retrieves service information from the SAs or DAs. The key words MUST, SHOULD, OPTIONAL and so on are used as described in RFC 2119.
sections.eli5: The UA is you asking questions, the SA is a shopkeeper describing what is for sale, and the DA is a notice board that collects descriptions from many shops.

sections.title: The Attribute List Extension
sections.content:
The extension has Extension ID = 0x0002 followed by a Next Extension Offset, a Service URL Length and Service URL, an Attribute List Length and Attribute List, a count of attribute authentication blocks (the AttrAuths count) and the blocks themselves if present. The Next Extension Offset is the position of the next extension, measured from the start of the SLP message. A value of 0 means there are no more extensions.

The Service URL identifies which URL Entry in the Service Reply the attributes belong to. The Attribute List field holds the entire attribute list of that service.
sections.eli5: It is a small label stuck onto the reply. It says which service it is about and lists everything that service can do.

sections.title: Asking and Answering
sections.content:
A UA sends an empty Attribute List Extension with its Service Request: the Service URL Length and Attribute List Length are 0 and those two fields are omitted. This asks the SA or DA to include an Attribute List Extension in its Service Reply.

An agent that supports the extension returns one Attribute List Extension for every URL Entry in the Service Reply. The order of the extensions SHOULD match the order of the URL Entries. The attributes must be in the same language as that indicated in the Service Request.

Support is OPTIONAL. An agent that does not support it just returns an ordinary Service Reply. The extension was given an identifying number from the range that tells a receiver it MUST ignore an unrecognized extension, so older implementations are not broken.
sections.eli5: You hand over an empty form. A helper who knows the trick fills in one form for each service found. A helper who does not know it just hands back the plain answer.

sections.title: Falling Back When Unsupported
sections.content:
If the UA receives a Service Reply without an Attrlist Extension, it must assume the SA or DA does not support the extension. The UA then has to send an Attribute Request for each URL it obtained in the Service Reply to learn the attributes of those services.

So the extension is purely an optimization. A client that uses it works against any SLPv2 agent, and only gains the saved round trips where the agent supports it.
sections.eli5: If the answer comes back without the extra details, you just go and ask for them the old way, one by one.

sections.title: Authentication and Languages
sections.content:
If the Service Request includes an SLP SPI string, the Attribute List Extension MUST include an authentication block. If the SA or DA cannot return an authentication block for that SPI, it MUST NOT return an Attribute List Extension. The blocks have exactly the same format as in an Attribute Reply or Service Registration message.

The RFC says SLPv2 already lets authenticators be returned with attribute lists so that UAs can verify a digital signature over the attributes, and the extension reuses that mechanism. It concludes that the extension is no less secure than SLPv2 without it. Language tagging works the same way: the existing SLPv2 mechanism for explicit language tags is reused.
sections.eli5: If you ask for a signed answer, you only get the details if they come with a signature. Otherwise you get nothing extra, never an unsigned guess.

fields.name: Next Extension Offset
fields.desc: Position of the next extension from the start of the SLP message; the offset continues in the next octet.

fields.name: Offset, contd.
fields.desc: Rest of the Next Extension Offset; 0 means no more extensions.

fields.name: Service URL Length
fields.desc: Length of the Service URL; 0 in a request.

fields.name: Service URL
fields.desc: Variable length; identifies the URL Entry the attributes belong to.
